project.name: OPlague
project.scope: Windows-first, read-only device inventory and driver-package diagnostics workbench for PnP, INF/ZIP, UDRV, snapshots, and evidence-led inspection.
project.safety_boundary: Device inventory and diagnostics remain read-only. Driver installation/modification and package execution are out of scope. Imported packages are untrusted input; exact hardware-ID matches are evidence for review, not automatic compatibility verdicts. Device identifiers retain existing pseudonymization and consent controls.

controls.intent: Align acceptance criteria and observed outcomes.
controls.remediation: Choose one authoritative contract; reconcile source, tests, and documentation; add a regression test for the corrected behavior.
controls.verification: Run focused tests and compare observable output with the written acceptance criteria.

controls.intent: Restore reliability when recovery, state, or error handling is inconsistent.
controls.remediation: Trace the failure to its root cause, add explicit bounds and failure handling, and preserve recoverable state.
controls.verification: Exercise boundary, timeout, failure, and recovery paths with deterministic tests.

controls.intent: Close unsafe or ambiguous input and permission paths.
controls.remediation: Reject malformed or untrusted input early; require explicit consent for sensitive actions; retain least privilege.
controls.verification: Add negative tests for malformed input, unauthorized operations, path traversal, and unintended side effects.

controls.intent: Modernize stale interfaces without breaking supported consumers.
controls.remediation: Introduce versioned contracts and migration notes; preserve promised compatibility; remove obsolete paths only after evidence.
controls.verification: Run compatibility tests against supported versions and build targets.

controls.intent: Prioritize high-value work and remove accidental complexity.
controls.remediation: Rank changes by impact, risk, and frequency; simplify duplicated steps without removing safeguards.
controls.verification: Compare task flow, measurable outcomes, and regression results before and after the change.

controls.intent: Align modules and dependencies around clear ownership.
controls.remediation: Define module boundaries and sources of truth; remove duplicate ownership and hidden cycles.
controls.verification: Run integration tests and verify each public contract has one authoritative owner.

controls.intent: Direct effort toward the project's primary outcomes.
controls.remediation: Prioritize the Windows read-only device and package-diagnostics workflow; keep unrelated integrations explicitly out of scope until supported by evidence.
controls.verification: Review roadmap items against implemented PnP inventory, INF/ZIP inspection, UDRV validation, metrics, and evidence-led reporting.

controls.intent: Make disputed design decisions explicit and evidence-led.
controls.remediation: Record options, trade-offs, decision ownership, and the selected contract instead of hiding disagreement in implementation.
controls.verification: Verify the documented decision against code and add tests for the selected behavior.

controls.intent: Rebuild fragile structures at a stable boundary when local patches accumulate.
controls.remediation: Consolidate duplicate logic behind a narrow module interface; avoid broad rewrites without characterization tests.
controls.verification: Run end-to-end and regression tests across every migrated path.

controls.intent: Refactor for clarity while preserving externally observable behavior.
controls.remediation: Use small changes, retain report/schema/UI contracts, and pair each refactor with focused tests.
controls.verification: Compare behavior and public interfaces before and after; run the relevant test suite.

controls.intent: Re-evaluate assumptions when the current design no longer serves supported workflows.
controls.remediation: Document the assumption, validate it against source and actual use, and change only what the evidence disproves.
controls.verification: Add tests for the revised behavior and document any changed defaults or migration steps.

controls.intent: Keep versions, schemas, documentation, and configuration synchronized.
controls.remediation: Use explicit versioned migrations and reject unsupported inputs with actionable errors.
controls.verification: Test current and supported legacy formats, including migration and round-trip behavior.

controls.intent: Transform data and workflows without losing provenance or meaning.
controls.remediation: Preserve source identity, normalized IDs, units, ordering, bounds, and error context; make lossy conversion explicit.
controls.verification: Use integrity, round-trip, normalization, and provenance tests.

controls.intent: Combine complementary capabilities without hidden coupling.
controls.remediation: Keep optional integrations behind explicit adapters and compatibility gates.
controls.verification: Test with optional integrations enabled and absent; core read-only inventory and inspection must remain stable.

controls.intent: Strengthen weak points revealed by repeated failures.
controls.remediation: Fix the highest-leverage root cause rather than repeatedly patching symptoms; add diagnostics where they improve evidence.
controls.verification: Reproduce the old failure and prove the regression test fails before and passes after the fix.

controls.intent: Finish edge cases before marking a capability complete.
controls.remediation: Close parser error paths, archive traversal, cancellation, cleanup, resource limits, empty states, and accessibility gaps.
controls.verification: Run boundary, malformed-package, cancellation, empty-state, cleanup, and platform-specific checks.

controls.intent: Improve clarity and accessibility without changing task semantics.
controls.remediation: Use clear hierarchy, labels, focus states, reduced motion, and understandable evidence/status feedback.
controls.verification: Check keyboard navigation and accessibility; confirm displayed status matches the underlying evidence.

controls.intent: Tune performance and precision using measured evidence.
controls.remediation: Profile representative inventory and package-inspection workloads, optimize demonstrated bottlenecks, and preserve exact-match behavior.
controls.verification: Record reproducible measurements and correctness comparisons; do not infer driver compatibility from performance scores.

controls.intent: Evolve architecture incrementally while retaining supported compatibility.
controls.remediation: Version report and package interfaces; provide migration paths and deprecation policy without weakening safety.
controls.verification: Test supported old and new package/report versions and migration paths where applicable.

controls.intent: Review emergent issues across modules, builds, tests, security, documentation, and repositories.
controls.remediation: Reconcile device inventory, package inspection, evidence, privacy, UI, and federation contracts; prioritize by risk and retain evidence.
controls.verification: Run all relevant CI gates and inspect cross-repository integration evidence before promotion.
